subject: SAML assertion lineage and owner-claim pack request
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@lunahealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: security@lunahealth.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SAML assertion lineage + owner-claim examples for SOC 2 intake

Hi Mateo / Irene,

As part of our SOC 2 evidence intake for Redwood (quarterly review), our internal audit team needs a small pack illustrating SAML assertion lineage and owner-claim mapping for a representative tenant. Specifically we need: 

- A few production-style SAML assertion samples (redacted PII) showing attributes used for mapping (email, groups, role).
- A short mapping table that explains which assertion attribute maps to which RBAC role in Redwood (owner, admin, service-account).
- Evidence of SCIM sync samples for the same tenant (delta + full sync) covering recent changes.
- IDP metadata and assertion signature verification note (how you verify signature + validation TTL).

Can you provide the pack by next Tuesday (2027-05-25)? KPMG will use the samples to validate your mapping logic and to confirm least-privilege enforcement on role changes.

We're happy to accept a Drive folder link or zipped artifact. If anything here is tricky from your side, please let us know the earliest ETA.

Thanks,
Alex Mercer
Security Manager, Luna Health

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@lunahealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SAML assertion lineage + owner-claim examples for SOC 2 intake

Alex — thanks for the clear list. We'll assemble a compact evidence pack that covers each bullet. Quick notes / clarifying Qs: 

1) Scope: we'll produce samples scoped to a test tenant that mirrors Luna's provisioning pattern (group-based RBAC + service-account roles). Does that work for KPMG validation, or do you need an exact Luna tenant export?

2) Redaction: samples will have email local-parts hashed and user IDs replaced, but group names and role labels will be preserved so mapping logic remains observable.

3) SCIM: we can include the most recent full export plus the delta containing the role assignment change that triggered a permission drop (timestamped). If you need the SCIM audit log entries as well, please confirm.

4) Signing verification: we'll include the IdP metadata (xml), the cert fingerprint, and a short note on the validation steps we run in the runtime (signature chain -> cert TTL check -> audience/recipient matching).

I'll aim to drop the pack into a Drive folder by EOD Monday (2027-05-24) so you have a day to review before Tuesday. CC'ing Irene and Jordan to align on what we drop.

Action items for us:
- Marissa: collate SCIM export and delta; produce scim-sync-snapshot-YYYYMMDD.json
- Irene: extract 3 representative SAML assertions and sign-off redaction
- Jordan: draft mapping table + brief narrative describing how role changes propagate to authorization decisions and any fallback/min-priv enforcement.

Mateo
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@lunahealth.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, soc2_kpmg@example.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SAML assertion lineage + owner-claim examples for SOC 2 intake

Alex / KPMG team — final pack has been uploaded and shared to the Drive folder linked below. Summary of contents: 

- saml-assertion-samples.csv (3 redacted assertions: initial login assertion, group-sync assertion, service-account-token assertion). Columns: timestamp, issuer, subject_hash, attributes(email_hash, groups, roles), signature_valid (true/false).
- idp-metadata.xml (IdP federation metadata; cert fingerprint included in metadata_comment.txt).
- scim-sync-snapshot-20270518.json (full export) + scim-delta-20270518.csv (delta events)
- mapping-table.csv (attribute -> RBAC mapping, includes example rows showing how group names map to Redwood roles and how inference runtime resolves multiple group claims)
- verification-notes.txt (steps to validate assertion signature, audience, recipient, and token replay protection)

Key points for auditors:
- Redactions: user identifiers are one-way hashed; group and role labels preserved for traceability.
- Lineage: we included the SCIM delta that shows the role removal event; mapping-table.csv demonstrates the runtime evaluation that resulted in reduced privileges (audit timeline included).
- Least privilege: we call out two safeguards — on-update validation (policy gate that rejects direct role elevation without owner approval) and session TTL enforcement for elevated sessions.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1LunaSecurityEvidence

If you (KPMG) want a walkthrough call to step through any assertion detail, happy to schedule.

Best,
Irene Choi
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Quoted message threads preserved above where applicable. Attachments referenced as stubs in the Drive folder for secure sharing.
